5. Identify the wrong statement among the following.
(a) In solids, molecules are closely packed.
(b) In solids, molecules have very strong intermolecular forces of attraction.
(c) In solids, molecules have only vibratory motion about their mean
positions.
(d) In solids, molecules possess very high kinetic energy.
(d) In solids, molecules possess very high kinetic energy.

6. The various steps involved in the process of condensation are given below.
Arrange them in a proper sequence.
(A) Further extraction of heat results in the decrease in potential energy of
molecules, whereas kinetic energy remains constant.
(B) The gas molecules, on cooling, lose heat energy which decreases the
kinetic energy as well as potential energy of the molecules.
(C) Increase in the forces of attraction results in the conversion of state.
(D) Decrease in potential energy leads to increase in intermolecular forces of
attraction.
(a) ABCD (b) BADC (c) BACD (d) ABDC

7. Identify the correct statement among the following.
(a) Boiling point of liquid decreases with increase in external pressure.
(b) Boiling point of liquid decreases by adding impurities.
(c) Addition of impurities to the solids decreases the melting point of solids.
(d) Addition of impurities to the solids increases the melting point of solids.

8. Conduction of heat is not possible through gases. Why?
(a) Gas molecules are very loosely packed.
(b) Gas molecules possess vibratory, rotatory and translatory motions.
(c) Gas molecules possess very high kinetic energy.
(d) Gas molecules are highly diffusable.

9. In which among the following cases is evaporation not involved?
(a) Skin becomes rough in winter.
(b) An earthen pot keeps water cool.
(c) In early winter morning, exhaled air appears foggy.
(d) Cool sensation is perceived when perfume is sprayed on the palms.
